subject: SLA template: monthly remedy structure & latency band exception (Greenfield)
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@greenfield.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: Greenfield Contracts <contracts@greenfield.ai>, Tom Wexler <tom.wexler@greenfield.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: SLA template discussion for our pilot — monthly credits and latency carveouts

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the throughput numbers look promising. Before we go deeper into a pilot commitment, our procurement and SRE teams asked me to run one more ask by you on the SLA template. Two items they want clear in the contract:

1) Monthly uptime target and remedy: Greenfield typically asks for 99.95% uptime for production tiers and a simple monthly service credit schedule (thresholds and percentage payout).

2) Latency bands: because our workloads include sporadic heavy batch ingest (model refreshes and embeddings backfills), we need either an explicit maintenance carveout for scheduled model refresh windows or an agreed latency-band credit calculation tied to p95/p99 latency windows.

I've attached a redline of Redwood's standard SLA with our comments (Greenfield_SLA_Redlines_v2.pdf) and a short spreadsheet with a suggested latency-banding approach (latency-banding-proposal.xlsx). Can Redwood consider a temporary exception for scheduled model-refresh windows (up to 6 hours/month) but keep the uptime target at 99.95 if we accept a reduced credit cap?

Goal is to align on something simple so legal can move forward. Happy to set a quick call tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Elena
Head of Infrastructure Partnerships
Greenfield AI

Attachments: Greenfield_SLA_Redlines_v2.pdf, latency-banding-proposal.xlsx

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena.park@greenfield.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: SLA template discussion for our pilot — monthly credits and latency carveouts

Elena — thanks for the note and the clear artifacts. We appreciate the detailed context. High level reaction: we can be flexible, but there are trade-offs that affect pricing and operational commitments. A few thoughts up front:  

- Redwood standard hosted SLA (for production tiers) is 99.9% uptime with the remedy ladder you saw. Moving to 99.95% is feasible but typically requires either reserved capacity or a higher commitment (we can discuss a blended reserved/dedicated pilot).

- For latency we can offer a latency-banding remedy tied to p95 and p99 for inference requests (not background batch jobs), OR we can accept a scheduled maintenance carveout that explicitly allows up to X hours/month for model refresh/backfills. The carveout would not count against uptime but we would exclude those windows from latency remedy calculations.

I attached an internal strawman (Greenfield-Redwood-MAP.docx) that sketches two options: (A) 99.9% uptime + 8h/month maintenance carveout + p99-based partial credits for real-time traffic; (B) 99.95% uptime with a monthly credit cap increase and requirement for a 3-month minimum reserved capacity commitment. Option B pushes more cost to you but reduces operational exceptions.

If you want to keep the credit cap constrained (your ask), Option A with a negotiated limited carveout (we can consider up to 6h/month) is the most straightforward. I'll loop our legal and sales ops to get a quick sense on commercial adjustment.

Available for a call tomorrow at 3pm ET.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Greenfield-Redwood-MAP.docx

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@greenfield.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 11:17:00 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: SLA template discussion for our pilot — monthly credits and latency carveouts

Team — forwarding Greenfield's redlines and my strawman. Key asks: 99.95% uptime OR 6h/month maintenance carveout + latency-banding. Greenfield prefers 99.95 but is willing to trade a larger credit cap for carveouts. 

Questions I need help with from legal/commercial:
- Can we offer a 6h/month scheduled maintenance carveout (explicitly for model refresh/backfills) and keep hosted pricing? If yes, what language do we lock into the SLA to avoid broad carveouts?
- If we move to 99.95% uptime for this account, what revenue/commitment threshold does that require (ben)?
- For latency-banding, can we limit remedies to real-time API endpoints (i.e., exclude background batch jobs)? Also what measurement: p95 vs p99? (marissa please weigh in on operational measurability).

I put my recommended fallback: accept the 6h/month carveout, keep base SLA at 99.9% and add targeted latency-banding for real-time endpoints with a modest credit schedule (p95/p99 thresholds). That preserves hosted economics and avoids reserved capacity unless they push for 99.95.

Thanks — appreciate quick turn here as they want to start pilot in August.

Markus, all — quick notes from legal/ops:

1) Carveout window: we can include a scheduled maintenance carveout limited to documented, pre-scheduled model refresh windows (customer to provide a monthly maintenance calendar at least 7 days in advance). Max 6 hours/month is workable, but we will require that any single maintenance event not exceed 4 hours unless pre-authorized. This prevents open-ended month-long refresh claims.

2) Measurement boundaries: remedies for latency should be scoped to "real-time inference API routes" (we should enumerate route prefixes in an appendix). Agreed measurement: p95 for a soft credit and p99 for a harder credit trigger. Credits will be token-based (percentage of monthly invoice) rather than per-request monetary fines.

3) Uptime: moving from 99.9% to 99.95% for hosted would normally require reserved capacity. If Greenfield is unwilling to accept reserved capacity, we can offer 99.95% as a time-limited concession (3-month pilot) with a right to revert to 99.9% without penalty. If they want the higher uptime for the contract term, we'd need to add a capacity commitment or price uplift.

Commercial — Ben, please advise on proposed credit caps and margin impact for option A vs B.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Park <elena.park@greenfield.ai>

Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 15:40:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: SLA template discussion for our pilot — monthly credits and latency carveouts

Markus / Laura — thanks, that framing helps. A couple of counterpoints from our side: 

- Greenfield prefers the 99.95% uptime for production because our customer SLAs require it; a time-limited pilot concession won't be sufficient long-term. We are open to a 3-month pilot with 99.9% while we validate, but contract must have a path to 99.95% tied to a modest reserved capacity commitment (we propose a 6-month revenue minimum rather than an immediate reserved cluster).

- On the maintenance carveout: the calendar approach is fine. We propose that scheduled model-refresh events be limited to two planned events/month unless otherwise agreed; unscheduled reprocessing due to data issues should not be considered maintenance.

- Credit cap: Greenfield is ok with a monthly credit cap but proposes a cap at 25% of monthly invoice for the first year, stepping down to 15% thereafter if we add monitoring/reporting obligations on both sides.

Next steps: we'd like to get a commercial sketch (blended pilot price + what it would cost to move to 99.95% with a 6-month minimum) and a revised SLA with the maintenance calendar language. Can Ben/Markus provide a quick commercial sketch and updated doc by EOD Tuesday? We'll try to get procurement sign-off the same week.

Best,
Elena

Attachments referenced: Greenfield_SLA_Redlines_v2.pdf, latency-banding-proposal.xlsx
